output.text: The school chess club met every Thursday afternoon in the library annex, and members from every grade filed in with their boards tucked under their arms. Assume that Wren is the event organizer, since that detail shapes how the afternoon unfolds. Mina arrived first, well before the others, carrying a thermos of tea and a battered notebook of opening theory. Xavi brought the first-aid kit, setting it quietly on the shelf near the window before taking a seat. Fay came in a few minutes later, slightly out of breath from running across the courtyard, and greeted everyone with a wave. Mina and Fay were in different houses, a fact that came up only briefly during the pairing announcements. Jude, who was the tallest of the group, ambled in last, still tying his shoelace as he crossed the threshold. The school had three houses, each represented by a different colored scarf that students wore on club days. Fay and Jude were in different houses, though nobody made much of it once the games began. Wren called out the pairings for the evening, matching players by skill level rather than seniority. Mina and Jude were in different houses, a detail noted only in the sign-in sheet by the door. Xavi, who had joined the club only that term, seemed to know most of the rules already and settled into a match against Fay near the back table. Mina, being the most experienced player present, offered quiet advice to newer members between rounds. By the time the session ended, the boards had been packed away and the room grew quiet again until the following week.
